summary: The Nutrition First Act of 2026 amends the Food and Nutrition Act of 2008 to bar SNAP benefits from purchasing soda, candy, high-sugar beverages, sugary desserts or snacks, and energy drinks by redefining eligible foods to exclude those items.

scores.thoughts: The bill amends SNAP rules to restrict eligible purchases but does not alter appropriation levels, program funding, or overall federal outlays. It has no direct bearing on the amount of government spending.
The bill contains no tax provisions, rate changes, credits, or revenue measures of any kind.

While improved nutrition can indirectly affect health outcomes, the bill is strictly a modification of SNAP purchase rules and does not address insurance coverage, medical care delivery, or healthcare policy.
No provisions related to firearms, regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
No provisions addressing immigration status, visas, border policy, or pathways to citizenship.
No provisions concerning reproductive health services or abortion access.
No provisions concerning defense budgets, military programs, or national security spending.
No provisions related to environmental regulations, emissions, or conservation policy.

The bill directly amends the Food and Nutrition Act to narrow the definition of eligible foods under SNAP, explicitly excluding soda, candy, energy drinks, and high-sugar/sodium snacks. This imposes new restrictions on program benefits, constituting a moderate tightening of the food assistance safety net.
No provisions concerning schools, school funding, curriculum, or education policy.
No provisions concerning controlled substances, decriminalization, or drug enforcement.
No provisions concerning sentencing, policing, or criminal justice reform.
No provisions concerning tariffs, trade agreements, or import/export policy.
The bill does not address deficits, debt ceilings, or fiscal targets.
No provisions concerning LGBTQ+ legal protections or related civil rights.
No provisions concerning foreign assistance or international aid.
No provisions concerning voting access, election administration, or voter ID.
No provisions concerning technology regulation, data privacy, or digital oversight.
No provisions concerning workers' rights, union organizing, or labor standards.
No provisions concerning religious exemptions or anti-discrimination rules.
